lesson_title: Value of ADE — Statutory Bounds & Principles
driving_rule_concept: Foundational philosophy of reduced-risk driving and TDLR ADE-1317 program expectations.
instructional_rationale: Administrative orientation and statistical overview of the Texas Adult Driver Education system. Abstract philosophy on crash statistics does not benefit from animated vehicle motion.
key_statutes_cited: Texas Transportation Code § 545.060; TTC § 545.104; Texas Administrative Code § 84.500.; TEXAS TRANSPORTATION CODE § 545.151; Texas Transportation Code § 545.151
relevant_assessment_question: Which vehicle demonstrates the legally correct lane positioning prior to the stop line?

lesson_title: Traffic Laws — Framework for Responsible Driving
primary_heading: Traffic laws create the framework for responsible driving
driving_rule_concept: Traffic laws provide the statutory framework for shared public roadway safety.
instructional_rationale: Explains traffic laws as a societal contract and Texas legal hierarchy. A static 2.5D schematic of an orderly urban grid (already present) conveys the concept of order vs chaos without motion.
relevant_assessment_question: Who has the legal right-of-way to proceed first?

lesson_title: Driving is a Privilege — Risk & Consequences
primary_heading: Driving is a privilege, not a constitutional right
driving_rule_concept: Driving is a state-regulated revocable privilege conditioned on legal compliance.
instructional_rationale: Legal distinction between constitutional rights and driving privileges. Conceptual and text-based legal principle; motion graphics would be decorative rather than instructional.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 521.292; Texas Transportation Code § 521; TTC § 521.; TTC § 601.051; TTC § 521; Texas Transportation Code § 521.292; TTC § 545.351; TTC § 521.001
relevant_assessment_question: Texas Move Over/Slow Down Act, what must a driver do when passing a stationary emergency or TxDOT vehicle with flashing lights on a 70 mph highway?

lesson_title: Obtaining, Possessing & Renewing a Texas DL
primary_heading: Your License to Drive: Statutory Qualifications & Custody
driving_rule_concept: Driver licensing statutory qualifications, residency requirements, and DPS application procedures.
instructional_rationale: Procedural administrative steps to apply for, test for, and renew a Texas driver license at DPS. Flowcharts and text checklists are optimal.
relevant_assessment_question: How many days does a new resident have to secure a Texas driver license after establishing residency in the state?

primary_heading: License Types, Restrictions, Endorsements & Special Info
driving_rule_concept: Vehicle weight thresholds defining Class A, B, and C driver licenses and statutory restriction codes.
instructional_rationale: Classification of Texas license classes (A, B, C, Commercial, M), restriction codes (e.g. corrective lenses), and anatomical gift registry. Best taught via a static visual reference card.
relevant_assessment_question: Which vehicle combination is legally authorized to be operated under a standard Texas Class C driver license?

driving_rule_concept: Mandatory suspensions, administrative license revocations (ALR), and court suspension cascades.
instructional_rationale: Statutory legal grounds for license suspension, revocation, and cancellation (TTC § 521.292). A structured flowchart mapping violations to sanction periods is clearer than motion.
relevant_assessment_question: What criminal charge applies to an individual operating a vehicle while their driver license is suspended, with prior convictions?

driving_rule_concept: Mandatory annual vehicle equipment inspection and registration verification under TTC § 548.
instructional_rationale: Annual vehicle safety inspection points (brakes, lights, wipers, horn) and Texas Two Steps One Sticker system. A static callout diagram of vehicle inspection points is ideal.
relevant_assessment_question: Under the Texas 'Two Steps, One Sticker' program, what prerequisite must be verified before vehicle registration renewal?

primary_heading: Financial Responsibility: The Safety Responsibility Act
driving_rule_concept: Mandatory liability insurance coverage limits: $30,000 bodily injury/person, $60,000/crash, $25,000 property damage.
instructional_rationale: Texas Safety Responsibility Act minimum liability thresholds (30/60/25). An insurance card schematic with financial coverage breakdown conveys the legal mandate clearly.
relevant_assessment_question: Which document is legally recognized as valid evidence of financial responsibility in Texas?

primary_heading: Reducing Roadway Risk: Legal Foundation Synthesis
driving_rule_concept: Consolidation of vehicle ownership, registration maintenance, and legal document retention.
instructional_rationale: Review and behavioral consolidation of licensing and vehicle compliance responsibilities. Text and checklist format sufficient.
relevant_assessment_question: How does maintaining current vehicle inspections and proper registration directly contribute to roadway risk reduction?

primary_heading: Texas Driving with Disabilities: Communication Protocols
driving_rule_concept: Voluntary disclosure of communication impediment on Texas driver licenses and law enforcement TLETS integration.
instructional_rationale: Samuel Allen Law and Texas Driving with Disabilities indicator. A high-clarity static illustration of a Texas driver license with the communication impediment endorsement is sufficient.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 545.151; Texas Transportation Code § 502.061; TTC § 521.142; TTC § 502.061
relevant_assessment_question: ON PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES", "prompt": "What is the primary mission of the Texas Driving with Disabilities Program during roadside traffic stops?

driving_rule_concept: At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the left must yield right-of-way to the vehicle on the immediate right.
instructional_rationale: Teaches fundamental intersection right-of-way under TTC § 545.151. Learners must see temporal sequence: two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled 4-way intersection; the driver on the left yields, waiting for the driver on the right to clear.
relevant_assessment_question: Under Texas statutory driving rules, what is the fundamental legal nature of the right-of-way?

driving_rule_concept: Vehicles on terminating roads at T-intersections and vehicles on unpaved roads must yield to through traffic.
instructional_rationale: T-intersections (TTC § 545.153) and unpaved vs paved road intersections. Motion is required to demonstrate vehicle on the terminating street coming to a complete halt, waiting for through-traffic in both directions to clear before turning.
relevant_assessment_question: At an uncontrolled T-intersection where one road terminates into a through street, who must yield?

driving_rule_concept: 4-way stop protocol (first-in-first-out) and modern roundabout entry yield rules.
instructional_rationale: 4-way stop order-of-arrival sequencing and roundabout circulation rules. Learners must observe the multi-car chronological sequence (first to stop, first to go; simultaneous arrival yields to right; entering traffic yields to circulating traffic in roundabouts).
relevant_assessment_question: If two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a two-way stop on opposing streets, who has right-of-way?

driving_rule_concept: Vacate adjacent lane when passing stopped emergency/utility vehicles with flashing lights, or slow down 20 mph below limit.
instructional_rationale: Texas Move Over / Slow Down Law (TTC § 545.157). Animation demonstrates a highway vehicle approaching a stationary police cruiser/tow truck on the shoulder, checking mirrors, indicating, and vacating the adjacent lane, or decelerating 20 mph below limit.
relevant_assessment_question: When an authorized emergency vehicle approaches with audible siren and flashing red/blue lights, what must you do?

driving_rule_concept: Mandatory stop for school buses with flashing red lights on undivided highways; physical median exception.
instructional_rationale: School bus red flashing lights and stop arm extension (TTC § 545.066). Animation clearly shows all lanes in both directions on an undivided roadway stopping, vs divided highway exception where opposing traffic separated by a physical median may proceed.
relevant_assessment_question: Which stationary vehicle type is protected under the expanded Texas Move Over/Slow Down Act?

driving_rule_concept: Unconditional duty to stop and yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and blind pedestrians with canes or service animals.
instructional_rationale: Right-of-way at pedestrian crosswalks (TTC § 545.061) and blind pedestrians with guide dog / white cane (TTC § 552.010). Animation demonstrates turning car yielding completely to crosswalk pedestrians before executing turn.
relevant_assessment_question: Why are right-of-way rules codified as legal duties rather than enforceable property rights in Texas?

driving_rule_concept: Defensive intersection entry: scanning all quadrants before accelerating on green to avoid red-light runners.
instructional_rationale: Defensive intersection management: clearing intersections (left-center-right-left scan) when light turns green, pausing 2 seconds, and detecting a red-light runner crossing illegally.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 545.061; TTC § 544.004); Texas Transportation Code § 545.061; TTC § 544.007(b); TTC § 552.008
relevant_assessment_question: Why are intersection collisions among the deadliest traffic events in Texas each year?

driving_rule_concept: Standardization of traffic control device shapes, colors, and legal meanings under the Texas MUTCD.
instructional_rationale: Road sign shapes (octagon, pennant, diamond, pentagon) and color codings (red, yellow, orange, green, blue, brown). Best learned via a structured, high-resolution static taxonomy chart.
relevant_assessment_question: A", "prompt": "What does a yellow diamond-shaped sign with a vehicle and wavy skid marks indicate to a Texas driver?

driving_rule_concept: Flashing yellow arrow indicates permissive left turn yielding to oncoming traffic; green arrow indicates protected turn.
instructional_rationale: Signal phase responses: protected green arrow vs permissive solid green ball vs flashing yellow arrow for left turns (TTC § 544.007). Motion is critical to show yielding to oncoming traffic during flashing yellow arrow vs protected right-of-way during green arrow.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 544.007; TTC § 545.055; TTC § 544.007(d); TTC § 544.008; Texas Transportation Code § 544.004.; TEXAS TRANSPORTATION CODE § 544.004; TTC § 544.004; Texas Transportation Code § 544.004
relevant_assessment_question: What does an illuminated steady yellow traffic light require an approaching driver to do in Texas?

driving_rule_concept: Pavement markings define legal passing zones, lane separation, and prohibited lane changes.
instructional_rationale: Pavement markings: broken yellow lines (passing allowed), solid yellow lines (no passing), double solid yellow, and solid white channelizing lines. Animated vehicle shows permitted vs illegal lane traversal.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 544.007(e); TEXAS TRANSPORTATION CODE § 544.002; TTC § 544.007; TTC § 544.002; TTC § 544.004; Texas Transportation Code § 544.006.; TTC § 544.005; Texas Transportation Code § 544.002
relevant_assessment_question: What is the legal status of an imitation traffic sign erected by a private citizen on public property?

driving_rule_concept: A dark or non-functioning traffic control signal must be operated as an all-way stop under TTC § 544.007(x).
instructional_rationale: Power outage / dark traffic signals: Texas law (TTC § 544.007(x)) explicitly mandates treating an inoperative electronic traffic signal as an all-way stop sign. Animation demonstrates 4 vehicles arriving at blacked-out signals and taking turns.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 544.007(e); TTC § 545.151; TTC § 542.404; TTC § 544.004; TTC § 545.066; Texas Transportation Code § 545.151.; Texas Transportation Code § 545.151
relevant_assessment_question: Why are warning signs placed significantly in advance of physical roadway hazards on Texas highways?

driving_rule_concept: The Texas Basic Speed Rule mandates driving at a speed that is reasonable and prudent under prevailing conditions.
instructional_rationale: Basic speed rule definition (reasonable and prudent speed under existing conditions TTC § 545.351). Conceptual legal framework; specific applications covered in subsequent lessons.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 545.351); TTC § 545.104; Texas Transportation Code § 545.051; TTC § 545.051; TTC § 545.351; Texas Transportation Code § 545.351; TEXAS TRANSPORTATION CODE § 545.351; TTC § 545.363
relevant_assessment_question: How does Texas traffic engineering define optimal traffic flow along multi-lane highway corridors?

driving_rule_concept: Drivers must drive on the right half of the roadway; the left lane on multi-lane highways is reserved for passing.
instructional_rationale: Lane discipline and Texas 'Keep Right Except to Pass' statute (TTC § 545.051). Animation demonstrates cruising in right/center lanes, moving to left lane solely to overtake, and promptly signaling back to right.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 544.007; TTC § 542.501.; TTC § 545.151; TTC § 542.404; Texas Transportation Code § 542.501; TEXAS TRANSPORTATION CODE § 544.004; TTC § 544.004; Texas Transportation Code § 544.004
relevant_assessment_question: If a uniformed police officer manually directs traffic through an active red signal, what is your legal duty?

driving_rule_concept: Continuous turn signal must be given for not less than the last 100 feet before turning or changing lanes.
instructional_rationale: Turn and lane change signaling requirements (TTC § 545.104: continuous signal for at least 100 feet prior to turning/stopping) and hand signals. Shows vehicle activating indicator 100 ft prior to turning into intersection.
key_statutes_cited: Texas Transportation Code § 545.104; TTC § 545.104; TTC § 547.501; TTC § 545.104); Texas Transportation Code § 545.104(b); TTC § 545.060; TEXAS TRANSPORTATION CODE § 545.104; TTC § 545.107
relevant_assessment_question: If vehicle turn indicators fail, how must a Texas driver signal an intention to stop or suddenly decrease speed?

driving_rule_concept: Safe two-lane highway overtaking requires returning to lane before oncoming vehicle is within 200 feet.
instructional_rationale: Two-lane highway passing maneuver (TTC § 545.053: returning to right side before coming within 200 ft of oncoming vehicle) and parallel parking mechanics (curb clearance 6-18 inches TTC § 545.302). Animation of passing clearance is safety-critical.
relevant_assessment_question: What is the minimum legal distance a driver may park from an intersection stop sign or flashing beacon?

primary_heading: The Invisible Zone: Blind Spot Driving
driving_rule_concept: Mirrors alone do not eliminate blind spots; drivers must perform physical head checks before lateral movement.
instructional_rationale: Blind spot physics and BGE (Blindspot and Glare Elimination) mirror setting. Top-down / 2.5D animated camera visualizes rear-view cone, side-mirror cone, blind zones, and the critical over-the-shoulder head check.
relevant_assessment_question: How far does the rear blind spot (No-Zone) extend behind a large commercial freight tractor-trailer?

driving_rule_concept: The 3-second rule establishes minimum safe following buffer under ideal conditions; expands to 4+ seconds in rain.
instructional_rationale: 3-second following distance rule (4 seconds in adverse conditions). Animation shows lead vehicle passing an overhead sign or shadow, an animated 3-second counter, and the following car reaching the landmark at the 3.00s mark.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 545.062.; Texas Transportation Code § 545.062.; TTC § 545.062; TTC § 545.351)
relevant_assessment_question: How does a Texas motorist accurately measure a three-second following distance interval?

primary_heading: Speed Related to Stopping: Roadway Conditions
driving_rule_concept: Braking distance increases quadratically with speed: doubling speed quadruples braking distance.
instructional_rationale: Stopping distance formula: Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Braking Distance = Total Stopping Distance. Animation compares braking distances at 30 mph, 50 mph, and 70 mph, showing exponential braking distance growth.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 547.302; TTC § 547.612; TTC § 545.351; Texas Transportation Code § 545.351; TTC § 545.351); TTC § 545.351(a)
relevant_assessment_question: When a vehicle's cruising speed doubles from 30 mph to 60 mph, how does its braking distance change?

lesson_title: Adjusting to Poor Conditions & Flash Floods
primary_heading: Adjusting to Poor Conditions & Flash Floods
driving_rule_concept: Hydroplaning causes complete loss of steering at speed; 6 inches of moving water can stall a vehicle and 12-24 inches can sweep it away.
instructional_rationale: Severe Texas weather hazards: hydroplaning mechanics at 35+ mph, flash flood low-water crossings ('Turn Around, Don't Drown'). Animation demonstrates tire riding on water wedge and vehicle stopping before flooded dip.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 545.352); Texas Transportation Code § 472.022; TTC § 472.022.; TTC § 472.022; TTC § 545.0541
relevant_assessment_question: How little moving water across a Texas low-water crossing is capable of carrying away a vehicle?

driving_rule_concept: Texas prima facie speed limits under TTC § 545.352 across urban, highway, and special designated corridors.
instructional_rationale: Statutory speed limit table (30 mph urban, 70/75 rural highway, 85 designated tollway, 15 alley, school zones). A clear comparative infographic is far more legible for study and memorization.
relevant_assessment_question: What is the statutory prima facie speed limit in a Texas urban district unless otherwise posted?

driving_rule_concept: Headlights required at darkness; dim high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 300 feet when following.
instructional_rationale: Vehicle lighting statutory rules (TTC § 547.302: lights on 30 min after sunset to 30 min before sunrise) and dimming requirements (low beams within 500 ft of oncoming, 300 ft following). 2.5D illumination cones demonstrate distance cutoffs.
relevant_assessment_question: At what distance must you dim your high-beam headlights when approaching an oncoming vehicle in Texas?

driving_rule_concept: Accelerate to highway speed on the ramp, merge smoothly into traffic gaps without stopping, and exit via deceleration lane.
instructional_rationale: Freeway entry acceleration lanes, gap selection, zipper merging, and exiting via deceleration lanes. Motion is essential to show matching freeway speed before merging, and rule to NEVER stop or reverse on freeway.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 545.401); TTC § 545.154); TTC § 545.415; TTC § 545.051; TTC § 545.154; TTC § 545.101; Texas Transportation Code § 545.154; Texas Transportation Code § 545.154.
relevant_assessment_question: What is the proper driver technique when traveling along a freeway entrance acceleration lane?

driving_rule_concept: Prevent highway hypnosis and drowsy driving by taking scheduled rest breaks every 2 hours or 100 miles.
instructional_rationale: Driver fatigue, circadian rhythms, micro-sleeps, and highway hypnosis prevention (take a break every 100 miles or 2 hours). Factual health guidance; animation is decorative.
relevant_assessment_question: What is 'highway hypnosis' and under what conditions does it typically affect long-distance drivers?

driving_rule_concept: Emergency shoulder pull-off protocol: activate hazard lights, exit passenger side, stand behind guardrail.
instructional_rationale: Vehicle breakdown on high-speed roadway: coasting to far right shoulder, hazard flashers, positioning behind guardrail, and deploying emergency reflectors/flares 100-200 feet behind.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 545.401); TTC § 547.305; Texas Transportation Code § 545.301; TTC § 545.301; Texas Transportation Code § 545.301.
relevant_assessment_question: If your vehicle breaks down on a high-speed Texas highway, where must you position the disabled car?

driving_rule_concept: In a tire blowout, hold steering wheel firmly, do not brake abruptly, ease off throttle, and pull safely to the right.
instructional_rationale: Tire blowout and mechanical failure recovery: do NOT slam brakes; grip wheel firmly, maintain straight path, ease off accelerator, steer gently onto shoulder once slowed.
relevant_assessment_question: If the rear wheels of your vehicle lose traction and skid to the right, how should you steer to recover?

primary_heading: Winter Driving Hazards, Bridges & Black Ice
driving_rule_concept: Overpasses freeze before roadway surfaces; steer into the direction of a skid without panic braking.
instructional_rationale: Winter driving: bridges and overpasses freeze first; skid recovery physics. Animation demonstrates vehicle rear skidding right on bridge deck and driver steering gently into the skid (to the right) without braking to recover traction.
relevant_assessment_question: Why do elevated highway bridges and overpasses in Texas freeze before adjacent roadway ground surfaces?

driving_rule_concept: Maintain space cushions ahead, behind, and on both sides to preserve escape paths from hazards.
instructional_rationale: Space cushioning and traffic harmonization: maintaining an open safety zone on all 4 sides of the vehicle, avoiding riding in dense clusters ('wolfpacks'), and establishing escape routes.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 542.404); TTC § 545.104; TTC § 545.062; TTC § 545.154; Texas Transportation Code § 545.062
relevant_assessment_question: What is the primary objective of managing a 360-degree 'space cushion' around your vehicle?

driving_rule_concept: Fines double in construction zones when workers are present; follow flaggers and obey lane closure merges.
instructional_rationale: Work zone safety and double fines law (TTC § 542.404). Animation demonstrates approaching highway construction zone, recognizing channelizing barrels, zipper merging early, and obeying human flagger stop/slow paddles.
key_statutes_cited: Texas Transportation Code § 542.404; TTC § 542.501); TTC § 545.353; TTC § 542.404; TTC § 472.022; TTC § 542.501
relevant_assessment_question: What is your legal obligation when encountering a designated human flagger in a Texas work zone?

driving_rule_concept: Loads must be tarped or tied to prevent cargo spillage; littering carries Class C to Class B misdemeanor fines.
instructional_rationale: Texas litter prevention laws (Health and Safety Code Ch. 365) and securing cargo loads under TTC § 725.021. Infographic on cargo tie-down requirements and litter fines is sufficient.
key_statutes_cited: Texas Transportation Code § 725.021; TTC § 725.021; TTC § 49.01); TTC § 725.021)
relevant_assessment_question: Under the Texas Litter Abatement Act, what is the penalty for littering up to 5 pounds on a highway?

lesson_title: Legal Definition of Intoxication in Texas
primary_heading: Legal Definition of Intoxication in Texas
driving_rule_concept: Intoxication is legally defined as alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, OR losing normal use of mental/physical faculties.
instructional_rationale: Texas legal definition of intoxication (Texas Penal Code § 49.01: 0.08 BAC OR lack of normal use of mental/physical faculties). A static legal matrix defining the dual statutory standard is crystal clear.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 522.101; Texas Penal Code § 49.01; Texas Penal Code §49.01; Texas Penal Code § 49.01(2)(B)
relevant_assessment_question: BAC) limit for adult drivers?

primary_heading: How Alcohol & Other Drugs Affect Driving Ability
driving_rule_concept: Alcohol and substances degrade visual acuity, judgment, reaction time, and peripheral perception.
instructional_rationale: Physiological impairment curves, peripheral vision tunneling, and synergistic drug effects. A high-clarity medical/physiological infographic is instructionally superior to moving animation.
relevant_assessment_question: At what constant rate does the human liver metabolize and eliminate alcohol from the bloodstream?

driving_rule_concept: DWI penalties escalate from Class B misdemeanor (1st offense) up to 2nd-degree felony for Intoxication Manslaughter.
instructional_rationale: Adult criminal penalties for Driving While Intoxicated (Texas Penal Code § 49.04, Intoxication Assault § 49.07, Intoxication Manslaughter § 49.08). Best structured as a statutory penalty matrix.
relevant_assessment_question: What are the statutory criminal penalties for a first-offense adult DWI conviction in Texas?

driving_rule_concept: Minors under 21 commit an offense with ANY detectable amount of alcohol in their system under Zero Tolerance.
instructional_rationale: Texas Zero Tolerance Law for minors (Alcoholic Beverage Code § 106.041: Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol with ANY detectable amount). A clear comparison chart between adult 0.08 and minor 0.00 standard is optimal.
suggested_animation_type: Static Minor vs Adult Comparison Graphic
relevant_assessment_question: Under the Texas Zero Tolerance law, what alcohol concentration triggers a DUI charge for a minor under 21?

driving_rule_concept: Open alcoholic beverage containers prohibited in the passenger area of a motor vehicle on public roadways.
instructional_rationale: Texas Open Container Law (Texas Penal Code § 49.031). A vehicle interior diagram illustrating illegal passenger area storage vs legal trunk/glovebox lockup conveys the statute perfectly.
key_statutes_cited: Texas Penal Code § 49.031; Texas Penal Code § 49.04(c); Texas Penal Code § 49.031.; Texas Penal Code § 49.031(a)(1); Texas Penal Code §49.031
relevant_assessment_question: Where may an open or unsealed container of alcohol be legally transported in a passenger car in Texas?

driving_rule_concept: Operating a motor vehicle implies consent to chemical testing; refusal triggers automatic 180-day license suspension.
instructional_rationale: Administrative License Revocation (ALR) and Texas Implied Consent Law (TTC § 724.011). Statutory flowchart illustrating blood/breath specimen test failure (90-day suspension) vs test refusal (180-day suspension).
relevant_assessment_question: What does the Texas Implied Consent law establish when a person operates a vehicle on public roads?

primary_heading: Reduce Risk: Zero Tolerance Practices & Impairment
driving_rule_concept: Practical personal strategies to eliminate impaired driving through designated drivers and planning.
instructional_rationale: Risk reduction strategies: designated driver selection, rideshare apps, peer intervention. Factual lifestyle planning; animation adds no technical instructional value.
relevant_assessment_question: What is the official definition of a true 'Designated Driver' according to Texas safety standards?

driving_rule_concept: Identification and differential vulnerability profiles of various road user classes.
instructional_rationale: Categorization of roadway users: pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists, heavy trucks, maintenance equipment. Visual reference taxonomy with vulnerability ratings is sufficient.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 547.008; TTC § 552.003; TTC § 552); TTC § 545.428; Texas Transportation Code § 545.428
relevant_assessment_question: Which category of roadway users is classified as 'vulnerable road users' under Texas traffic safety laws?

driving_rule_concept: Civil liability immunity for citizens rendering emergency care at the scene of an emergency in good faith.
instructional_rationale: Texas Good Samaritan Law (Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 74.151) protecting drivers who render emergency care at a crash scene in good faith. Legal statute text and bulleted guidelines.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 550.021); TTC § 550.023-024; TTC § 550.024; TTC § 550.021; Texas Transportation Code § 550.021
relevant_assessment_question: What is the criminal penalty under Texas law for fleeing the scene of a crash resulting in a fatality?

primary_heading: Laws for Sharing the Road: Bikes, Trucks & Horses
driving_rule_concept: Never pass a large commercial vehicle on the right when it is turning; stay clear of truck No-Zones.
instructional_rationale: Commercial vehicle blind spots ('No-Zones') and the dangerous 'right turn squeeze'. Animation demonstrates a tractor-trailer swinging left to turn right; a following car attempts to pass on the right and is trapped in the pinch zone.
key_statutes_cited: TTC § 542.003.; Texas Transportation Code § 551.101; TTC § 551.101; TTC § 542.003
relevant_assessment_question: What is the recommended safe passing distance when overtaking a bicyclist on a Texas roadway?

primary_heading: Responsibilities of a Defensive Driver: IPDE Process
driving_rule_concept: Maintain at least 3 feet of lateral clearance when passing cyclists and respect motorcycle right-of-way.
instructional_rationale: Principles of sharing the road with vulnerable users (cyclist 3-foot passing rule, motorcycle buffer). A clear diagram showing the 3-foot bicycle passing clearance envelope is optimal.
relevant_assessment_question: What are the four systematic stages of the IPDE defensive driving decision-making process?

driving_rule_concept: Statutory child restraint requirements, truck bed passenger restrictions, and hot car unattended child prohibitions.
instructional_rationale: Child passenger safety seat requirements (TTC § 545.412: under 8 or under 4'9"), open truck bed riding prohibitions (TTC § 545.414: under 18), and unattended children (Penal Code § 22.10). Infographic is superior.
relevant_assessment_question: Until what age and height must children be secured in an approved child safety seat system in Texas?

primary_heading: Responsibilities If Stopped by Law Enforcement
driving_rule_concept: Step-by-step procedural compliance during a police traffic stop to ensure safety of driver and officer.
instructional_rationale: Driver conduct during a law enforcement traffic stop: signal right, pull off safely to the right shoulder away from traffic, put vehicle in park, turn on interior dome light at night, keep hands visible at 10 and 2 on the steering wheel.
statutory_source_verification_required: Yes (Community Safety Education Act / TDLR Guidelines)
relevant_assessment_question: When a law enforcement officer activates emergency lights behind you, what is the proper pull-over procedure?

driving_rule_concept: Statutory rights and obligations during citizen-police interactions under the Community Safety Education Act.
instructional_rationale: Community Safety Education Act (Senate Bill 30 / 16 TAC § 84.500): mutual rights and responsibilities of citizens and peace officers, complaint and commendation procedures. A balanced legal rights matrix is most accurate.

driving_rule_concept: De-escalate aggressive road encounters: do not make eye contact, yield right-of-way, avoid retaliatory driving.
instructional_rationale: Aggressive driving and road rage de-escalation: handling aggressive tailgaters and confrontation. Animation demonstrates a driver staying calm, maintaining speed, indicating and shifting right to let the tailgater pass without escalation.
relevant_assessment_question: What key distinction separates aggressive driving traffic offenses from criminal 'road rage'?

driving_rule_concept: Trailers must be equipped with crossed safety chains capable of supporting the trailer if the hitch disconnects.
instructional_rationale: Towing and trailer equipment requirements (TTC § 545.409: safety chains crossed under tongue, hitch ratings, breakaway brake cables). A technical engineering cross-section diagram is clearest.

driving_rule_concept: Carbon monoxide is colorless, odorless, and deadly; never idle in enclosed garages or with blocked tailpipes.
instructional_rationale: Carbon monoxide poisoning risks: exhaust leaks, warming cars in enclosed garages, blocked tailpipes. Static cutaway diagram showing CO gas circulation hazards.
relevant_assessment_question: What physical sensory characteristics make carbon monoxide (CO) gas exceptionally dangerous?

primary_heading: Texas Move Over / Slow Down Act Statutes
driving_rule_concept: Mandatory obligation to display driver license and proof of financial responsibility upon peace officer demand.
instructional_rationale: Administrative compliance when requested by law enforcement: producing driver license, registration, and insurance. Pure procedural legal overview.
relevant_assessment_question: Under the Texas Move Over / Slow Down Act, what must you do if you cannot safely vacate the adjacent lane?

driving_rule_concept: Do not pass pilot vehicles or attempt to cut into oversize load convoys; yield right-of-way at bridges and pinch points.
instructional_rationale: Navigating near escorted oversize/overweight loads: pilot vehicles with flashing amber lights and 'OVERSIZE LOAD' signs, dynamic passing restrictions on two-lane roads. Motion shows respecting escort vehicle buffer.

relevant_assessment_question: What does a pilot escort vehicle with amber flashing lights and 'OVERSIZE LOAD' banner indicate?

driving_rule_concept: Overview of state program allowing drivers to record health conditions on license and vehicle registration.
instructional_rationale: Texas Driving with Disabilities Program detailed administrative framework (16 TAC § 84.500 / DPS guidelines). Program architecture overview diagram.

relevant_assessment_question: What is the primary statutory purpose of the Texas Driving with Disabilities Program?

lesson_title: How to Participate in the Program
